courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Introductory Interdisciplinary Topics in European Studies
courses.description: Analysis of various aspects of European culture, science, and technology. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted unless the topics vary: European Studies 302, 306, 307, 308. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Varies with the topic.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Introduction to European Studies
courses.description: The myths, ideas, and sociopolitical realities that underpin the intellectual and cultural construction of Europe. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Introductory Topics in European Anthropology, Geography, History, and Sociology
courses.description: Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted unless the topics vary: European Studies 302, 306, 307, 308. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Varies with the topic.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Introductory Topics in European Culture, Literature, Art, Music, and Media
courses.description: Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted unless the topics vary: European Studies 302, 306, 307, 308. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Varies with the topic.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: An Introduction to Western Music
courses.description: Same as Music 302L. Introduction to musical styles in the Euro-American art music tradition between the Middle Ages and the present day. Designed to foster critical listening and thinking about music, and deepen understanding of the vital role that music has played and continues to play in society and in individual lives. Three lecture hours a week for one semester, with one laboratory hour a week as required. Only one of the following may be counted: European Studies 307 (Topic: Introduction to Western Music), 307M, Music 302L.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Introductory Topics in European Economics, Government, Business, and Policy
courses.description: Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted unless the topics vary: European Studies 302, 306, 307, 308. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Varies with the topic.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Preparation for Study Abroad in Europe
courses.description: One lecture hour a week for one semester. May not be counted by students who have previously taken an international learning seminar. Offered on the pass/fail basis only.
courses.offering: Offered on the pass/fail basis only.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Continuity and Change in Modern France
courses.description: Same as French Civilization 340M. Focuses on various social, political, and cultural crises in France from the revolution of 1789 to the present time. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. European Studies 340M and French Civilization 340M may not both be counted. May not be counted toward fulfillment of the foreign language requirement for any bachelor's degree. Prerequisite: Upper-division standing.
courses.excluded: fulfillment of the foreign language requirement for any bachelor's degree

courses.title: Topics in European Anthropology, Geography, History, and Sociology
courses.description: Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted unless the topics vary: European Studies 346, 347, 348, 363. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Upper-division standing.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Topics in European Culture, Literature, Art, Music, and Media
courses.description: Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted unless the topics vary: European Studies 346, 347, 348, 363. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Varies with the topic.

courses.title: Topics in European Economics, Government, Business, and Policy
courses.description: Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted unless the topics vary: European Studies 346, 347, 348, 363. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Varies with the topic.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Governments and Politics of Western Europe
courses.description: Same as Government 324L. Comparative study of peoples, institutions, parties, interest groups, and bureaucracy in the countries of Western Europe, concentrating on the major political systems of Britain, France, Germany, and Italy. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. European Studies 350 and Government 324L may not both be counted. Prerequisite: Six semester hours of lower-division coursework in government.
courses.prereqText: Six semester hours of lower-division coursework in government.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Germany and Europe since 1945
courses.description: Restricted to students participating in the summer program in Wuerzburg, Germany. The equivalent of three lecture hours a week for one semester. Prerequisite: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Upper-division standing and consent of instructor.
courses.restricted: Restricted to students participating in the summer program in Wuerzburg, Germany.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Supervised Research
courses.description: Individual instruction. Prerequisite: Upper-division standing.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Independent Research in European Studies
courses.description: Tutorially directed research on a modern European topic. Conference course. Required for the concentration in European studies. May be repeated for credit. Prerequisite: Upper-division standing, admission to the European studies program, and consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Upper-division standing, admission to the European studies program, and consent of instructor.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Topics in European Studies
courses.description: An analysis of various aspects of European culture, science, and technology. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted unless the topics vary: European Studies 346, 347, 348, 363. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Varies with the topic.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Capstone Research in European Studies
courses.description: Supervised research on a modern European topic chosen in consultation with the student's adviser and culminating in a full-length thesis. Individual instruction. Prerequisite: Upper-division standing, admission to the European studies major, and consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Upper-division standing, admission to the European studies major, and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: EUS
courses.title: Advanced Topics in European Studies
courses.description: Examination of recent developments in Europe, with emphasis on the role of the European Union in political, cultural, economic, and security matters. Three lecture hours a week for one semester or as required by the topic. May be repeated for credit when the topics vary. Prerequisite: Graduate standing; additional prerequisites vary with the topic.
